title: bug: JetBrains Epic detail sends its typed edits and an Archived status in one UPDATE_EPIC frame and closes before the reply. Since 09529122 (task-625c7cfe) the daemon refuses that whole save for an epic with a PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL or WORKING row, so every typed edit is lost behind a raw "[NOT_ALLOWED] … via moe.set_task_status" balloon. On a quiet epic, the same combo pick archives every task with no confirmation
description:
Filed by hunt #14 (task-d5d58972, 2026-11-03, architect-1dd28c7c). This is the IDE follow-through on task-625c7cfe, and it was hunt #9's held item (b). JetBrains is first; the VS Code twin is held back until this row lands.

PROBLEM (HEAD 942717bc)
- The dialog and the frame:
  - moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/EpicDetailDialog.kt:31 offers ARCHIVED in the status combo unconditionally.
  - Save (:76-89) sends title, description, architectureNotes, epicRails and the chosen status in ONE frame through MoeCommandSender.updateEpicDetails (services/MoeCommandSender.kt:104-118).
  - It then calls close(OK_EXIT_CODE) (:88) before any reply.
- What the daemon does with it since 09529122:
  - /ws UPDATE_EPIC (packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts:677) calls applyEpicUpdate (tools/updateEpic.ts:37-52).
  - A move to ARCHIVED runs archive_epic FIRST (:50). The companion fields are written only after it succeeds (:51).
  - archive_epic refuses while any task of the epic is PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL or WORKING (tools/archiveEpic.ts:12 IN_FLIGHT, refusal at :61-67). That is all-or-nothing by design: the typed title, description, notes and rails are never written.
- What the human sees: MoeToolWindowPanel.kt:349-354 shows the raw ERROR text: "UPDATE_EPIC: [NOT_ALLOWED] archive epic not allowed: Epic "epic-…" has N in-flight task(s) (task-…:WORKING). Move them to BACKLOG first via moe.set_task_status (release_task keeps …)". It gives an epic id and task ids, not titles, and MCP instructions addressed to an agent. The dialog is already closed and the edits are gone.
- The success path:
  - archive_epic archives EVERY not-yet-archived task: BACKLOG, REVIEW (un-reviewed work included), DONE and BLOCKED (archiveEpic.ts, the loop after the in-flight gate).
  - One combo pick does that with no confirmation. The Delete button beside it confirms (EpicDetailDialog.kt:91-103).
  - Setting the epic back to ACTIVE later is a plain update that leaves its tasks ARCHIVED, and the board does not render ARCHIVED rows.
- Not affected: the epic-header drag never sends ARCHIVED (MoeToolWindowPanel.kt mapEpicStatus).

EVIDENCE
- Daemon side, the exact frame the dialog builds, against a real StateManager + MoeWebSocketServer on an ephemeral port. The repro is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-d5d58972/B/zzHuntB_clientFrames.test.ts (needs zzHuntB_harness.ts beside it), run from packages/moe-daemon/src/__hunt__/ of a `git archive 942717bc` snapshot. `npx vitest run src/__hunt__/zzHuntB_clientFrames.test.ts` → 3 passed, recording:
  HUNT DAEMON REPLY: {"type":"ERROR","message":"[NOT_ALLOWED] archive epic not allowed: Epic \"epic-1\" has 1 in-flight task(s) (task-working:WORKING). Move them to BACKLOG first via moe.set_task_status (release_task keeps a WORKING task in the WORKING column, so releasing does not make it archivable).","operation":"UPDATE_EPIC","code":-32003,"codeName":"NOT_ALLOWED","context":{"epicId":"epic-1"}}
- After the refusal the test asserts title 'Original title', description 'Original description' and status ACTIVE, so the typed edits were dropped. The control test (same frame, status left ACTIVE) lands the rename.
- The architect's re-run is in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-d5d58972/me/clientFrames.rerun.txt.

FIX DIRECTION (plugin only; the daemon's all-or-nothing archive stays as 625c7cfe designed it)
1. Decide locally, from the cached snapshot, before sending. Choosing Archived for an epic with a PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL or WORKING task sends nothing ARCHIVED. It shows a message listing those tasks by TITLE and saying they must leave those columns first.
2. Confirm the cascade: "Archive epic X and its N task(s)?", where N is the not-yet-ARCHIVED tasks. Cancel sends nothing.
3. Split the save. Send the field edits with the epic's CURRENT status first (updateEpicDetails), then the status change on its own through the existing MoeCommandSender.updateEpicStatus (:93-103) or an equivalent status-only frame. A stale-cache refusal can then never drop the typed edits; the existing balloon still reports it, which is acceptable.
Put the decision in a small pure helper (e.g. toolwindow/EpicArchive.kt) that takes the epic, its tasks and the chosen status, and returns the blockers, the cascade count and the frames to send. That makes it unit-testable without a dialog. New user-visible text goes in MoeBundle.properties, ASCII.

FILES (planner to confirm)
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/EpicDetailDialog.kt
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/EpicArchive.kt (new pure helper)
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties
- moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/EpicArchiveTest.kt (new)

OUT OF SCOPE: any daemon change (updateEpic.ts and archiveEpic.ts stay as they are); moe-vscode/** (the VS Code twin, EpicDetailPanel.ts:291 and :97-115, is held back until this lands); docs/MCP_SERVER.md, because no MCP contract changes. Docs: docs/PLUGIN_SPEC.md:21 and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:305 only name the dialog, so if a plugin doc describes the epic status combo, sync that line in this row.

VERIFICATION: under the jetbrains-gradle lease, `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test --tests 'com.moe.toolwindow.EpicArchiveTest'`, then the plain `./gradlew test` (a CI merge gate).
definitionOfDone: EpicArchiveTest proves the guard. An epic whose cached tasks include a PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL or WORKING row yields no ARCHIVED frame. The helper returns those tasks' TITLES (not ids) for the local message. With none in flight, it reports the cascade count of not-yet-ARCHIVED tasks.

EpicArchiveTest proves the split. Edited fields plus Archived produce a field-edit frame that keeps the epic's current status, BEFORE a separate status-only ARCHIVED frame. Edited fields with an unchanged non-ARCHIVED status still produce exactly one frame, as today.

EpicDetailDialog only sends ARCHIVED after a confirmation that states the task count, and Cancel sends nothing; the dialog calls the helper rather than building frames itself. Under the jetbrains-gradle lease, `./gradlew test --tests 'com.moe.toolwindow.EpicArchiveTest'` and the full `./gradlew test` both exit 0.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 3 wiring. In EpicDetailDialog.kt, replace the Save action's doAction body (HEAD lines 78-88, from `val newTitle =` through `close(OK_EXIT_CODE)`) with edits.md section 1's NEW block, verbatim. Then diff the file against ref/EpicDetailDialog.expected.kt (sha256 526dd899328272c7f2c0947518ad3b95445ea82179c45c78c09f8f5caed0a805); it must match byte for byte.

What the new Save does:
- It builds EpicEdits with today's normalization (trimmed, a blank title keeps the old one, blank rail lines dropped) and reads chosenStatus from the combo.
- It reads service.getState() once and plans from the NEWEST cached epic (`current`, falling back to the dialog's open-time `epic`) and the whole cached task list. Planning from the open-time copy alone would let an untouched ARCHIVED combo re-archive an epic that someone un-archived meanwhile, with no confirmation.
- It calls EpicArchive.save with three callbacks. warnInFlight: Messages.showWarningDialog with IN_FLIGHT_MESSAGE_KEY (epic.title, then one '- <title>' line per task) and TITLE_KEY. confirmArchive: Messages.showOkCancelDialog with CONFIRM_MESSAGE_KEY (epic.title and the count), 'Archive Epic' as title and OK text, moe.button.cancel as Cancel text and the warning icon, compared == Messages.OK. send: a when over EpicSaveFrame, where Details calls service.updateEpicDetails(epic.id, the edits, frame.status) and Status calls service.updateEpicStatus(epic.id, frame.status, frame.order).
- It closes only `if (sent)`. With tasks in flight, or on Cancel, nothing is sent and the dialog stays open with the typed edits, so the human can pick another status and Save, or cancel the dialog.

The source guard anchors on these exact strings, so keep them verbatim: `val state = service.getState()`, `val current = state?.epics?.firstOrNull { it.id == epic.id } ?: epic`, `EpicArchive.plan(current, state?.tasks.orEmpty(), edits, chosenStatus)`, `EpicArchive.save(`, `MoeBundle.message(EpicArchive.CONFIRM_MESSAGE_KEY, epic.title, count)`, `) == Messages.OK`, `send = { frame ->` and `if (sent) close(OK_EXIT_CODE)`. No `service.updateEpic` text, comments included, may appear before `send = { frame ->`, and the Save action holds exactly one `close(OK_EXIT_CODE)`.

No import changes: the new types share the package, and Messages is already imported. The status combo keeps all four entries, and the Delete and Cancel actions stay untouched. MoeCommandSender, MoeProjectService and MoeToolWindowPanel need no edit; the epic-header drag never sends ARCHIVED (mapEpicStatus).

Error handling: MoeCommandSender.sendMessage never throws, and a disconnected sender sends nothing and fires onDisconnected. When the cache lagged a task going in flight, the daemon refuses the ARCHIVED frame and the existing UPDATE_EPIC error balloon reports it, but only after the details frame has landed, so the typed edits are kept (mem:gotcha-epic-update-archive).

Docs: docs/PLUGIN_SPEC.md:21 and :51, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:305 and docs/UI_SPEC.md:15 only name the dialog, and no doc describes the status combo, so there is no doc edit. Out of scope: moe-vscode/** (its twin is held back), any daemon change, and docs/MCP_SERVER.md.

Focused run under the lease, released afterwards: EpicArchiveTest tests=13 failures=0 errors=0.

Step 3's full plugin suite is the regression gate: only moe-jetbrains changes, with no daemon, proxy, VS Code or docs change.

Mutants run under the jetbrains-gradle lease in a copy outside the checkout, never in the worktree, because a crash mid-mutant would land the mutant (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-qa-mutants-in-archive-copy, worker variant). Run `git archive HEAD moe-jetbrains | tar -x -C /mnt/d/moe-scratch/m-048b`, then `cp --parents` every path that `git status --porcelain -- moe-jetbrains` lists. - M1: delete plan()'s in-flight return. 'archiving with in-flight tasks sends nothing and names them by title' and 'each in-flight status alone blocks the archive' must fail.
- M2: the archive Details frame carries chosenStatus instead of epic.status (today's one-frame bug). 'a quiet epic sends its edits with the current status before a status-only ARCHIVED frame' and 'an epic with no tasks still asks with a zero count' must fail.

Also check by reading:

executionContract.intendedBehavior: The JetBrains Epic detail Save decides an Archived pick locally, from the newest cached board, before sending. With a PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL or WORKING task in the epic, it sends nothing, shows those tasks by title, and keeps the dialog open with the typed edits. Otherwise it asks 'Archive epic X and its N task(s)?', where N is the epic's not-yet-ARCHIVED tasks. Cancel sends nothing and keeps the dialog open. OK sends the field edits with the epic's current status, then a separate updateEpicStatus ARCHIVED frame, and closes the dialog. Any other status choice, or an epic that is already ARCHIVED, still sends exactly one frame, as today.
acceptanceCriteria: EpicArchive.plan returns no frames, plus the in-flight tasks' titles (not ids, in board order), when Archived is chosen for a not-yet-ARCHIVED epic with a PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL or WORKING task of that epic.
With none in flight it returns [Details(edits, the epic's current status), Status(ARCHIVED, the epic's order)], with archiveTaskCount equal to that epic's non-ARCHIVED tasks.
A non-ARCHIVED choice, or an already-ARCHIVED epic, returns exactly one Details frame with the chosen status.
EpicArchive.save warns and sends nothing for in-flight titles. It asks with the count before sending an archive, sends nothing on Cancel, and otherwise sends every frame in order.
EpicDetailDialog's Save calls EpicArchive.plan and EpicArchive.save, sends only through save's send callback, and closes only when save returns true.
Both Gradle runs in checkRefs exit 0 under the jetbrains-gradle lease; EpicArchiveTest has 13 tests and 0 failures.
invariants: No ARCHIVED frame is sent without a confirmation that quotes the task count.
The field-edit frame always precedes the ARCHIVED frame, so a daemon refusal never drops typed edits.
A locally refused or cancelled Save sends nothing and leaves the dialog open.
Only tasks of this epic count, and ARCHIVED rows never block the cascade or count toward it.
compatibility: No daemon, MCP or /ws contract change: the frames reuse MoeCommandSender.updateEpicDetails and updateEpicStatus unchanged.
A non-archive Save still sends one UPDATE_EPIC frame with every field and the chosen status.
The status combo keeps PLANNED, ACTIVE, COMPLETED and ARCHIVED.
moe-vscode is untouched; its twin is held back until this lands.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) A local refusal that still sends the typed edits and closes: rejected. It half-applies a Save the human never confirmed. Keeping the dialog open loses nothing and lets them choose another status; both readings meet DoD 1 (no ARCHIVED frame). 2) A source-order guard as the only proof of the dialog flow (DoneColumnClear style): replaced by BoardRelease's shape, a headless save() flow with UI callbacks, so 'Cancel sends nothing' is a behavioral test; a slim source guard pins only the wiring. 3) Planning from the dialog's open-time epic: rejected. An epic un-archived while the dialog is open would be re-archived by an untouched ARCHIVED combo with no confirmation, so Save reads the newest cached epic. 4) A new status-only sender without order: rejected as scope. The task names the existing updateEpicStatus (status plus the unchanged order), the same frame the epic-header drag sends. 5) A Kotlin test that reads archiveEpic.ts to pin IN_FLIGHT: rejected, because QA's archive-copy route extracts only moe-jetbrains and the test would throw there; the KDoc names the daemon source instead. 6) Skipping the details frame when no field changed: rejected. The extra frame is harmless, and an equality check could drop a whitespace-only edit.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The toolwindow pure helpers are BoardMoves, BoardApproval, BoardRelease (a pure flow plus an EDT adapter with callbacks) and DoneColumnClear. Tests are JUnit4 on a bare JVM: build.gradle.kts strips the IntelliJ platform from :test, so MoeBundle and DialogWrapper cannot run there, while internal declarations are visible from the test source set. WebSocketServer.sendStateSnapshot drops ARCHIVED tasks and epics from the plugin snapshot, so the cached board rarely holds ARCHIVED rows; plan() excludes them anyway. handlePluginMessage reaches the FIFO StateManager mutex before its first await, so one socket's frames apply in arrival order. MoeProjectService.getState() is cleared only in dispose(). Plugin Kotlin and bundle files are LF (.gitattributes eol=lf). The key moe.button.cancel (=Cancel) already exists.
planningNotes.risks: The reference bytes are uncompiled: on a compile failure, read the FIRST e: line, because the cascade hides the cause. The source guard depends on literal anchors: keep them verbatim, comments included. A cache that lags a task going in flight makes the daemon refuse the ARCHIVED frame (the existing balloon) after the edits landed; the task accepts that. Each archive Save emits two or three EPIC_UPDATED events (details, archive, and the order write that updateEpicStatus carries); accepted. Many long in-flight titles make a tall warning, and IntelliJ's Messages dialog scrolls long text. A transport drop between the two synchronous sends gets no handling beyond the existing onDisconnected path, and both sends pass the same connected check.
